long_biography.plain_text:
Raised in Nebraska, Hinrich studied business and mathematics before earning a graduate degree in international trade. He moved to Asia and learned trade publishing through work in Japan and across regional markets. In 1970, he co-founded Trade Media in Hong Kong and launched Asian Sources, connecting Asian manufacturers with Western buyers. The publisher later became Global Sources, adding digital marketplaces and trade exhibitions while retaining its business-to-business information model.

Global Sources listed on Nasdaq and remained controlled by Hinrich until its sale to a Blackstone affiliate in 2017. Securities filings identified shares held directly by him, separately held family shares and a foundation-linked block, preventing the combined percentage from being treated as solely personal. The transaction converted company shares into cash, but its total value was not Hinrich's personal proceeds. He now chairs the nonprofit Hinrich Foundation, which funds trade research and education. That position establishes continuing leadership and philanthropy, not a current wealth-producing industry. His undisclosed post-sale holdings therefore leave his present primary industry unknown; foundation assets likewise belong to the nonprofit.
